insights.insight: $4.62M in cryptographically verified purchase GMV across 86,634+ receipts establishes a deterministic commerce dataset at a scale where category and brand signals become statistically meaningful — not modeled inference, but confirmed transactions.

Pre-rollover 7-day GMV has crossed $100K on three consecutive days, with peaks of $101.3K, $102.2K, and $101.9K — confirming the $100K weekly threshold has shifted from ceiling to floor, signaling durable consumer engagement rather than a one-time spike.

The 14-day receipt pool spans grocery (28.5%), restaurants and dining (22.2%), department stores (16.8%), and gas/convenience (11.4%) — a four-vertical spread that maps to real household spend patterns and supports cross-category audience construction without single-vertical concentration risk.

Walmart (346 receipts), Kroger (161), Costco (156), Publix (135), and Home Depot (56) have each crossed independent visibility thresholds in the 14-day window, with Safeway, Aldi, Whole Foods, and Lowe's also confirmed — enabling competitive share-of-wallet analysis at the brand level from verified purchase data.

From approximately 37,576 receipts in late June to 86,634 by early October represents roughly 49,000 net new verified receipts over 108 days — a structural pace of ~454 receipts per day that has held without compression, indicating supply-side reliability for brands evaluating this as a targeting input.

Standard programmatic CPMs pay $5+ to infer purchase intent from behavioral proxies; a verified receipt confirms a transaction occurred, at a specific retailer, in a specific category — the gap between inference and cryptographic proof is the addressable efficiency gain for brands currently buying probabilistic audiences.
